```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

`ysx_check()` extends `yspec::ys_check()` with three checks that are driven by
the `dots` of each column in the specification:

| Check | `dots` setting | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Missing values | `na_ok` | `false`: missing values are not allowed |
| Rows per group | `group`, `pre_grp_count` | each group occurs once |
| Time-varying columns | `group`, `time_varying` | constant within each group |

Missing values must be coded as the specification's `missing_code`
(`SETUP__: missing_code`) when one is set.

```{r setup-spec}
library(yspecx)

spec <- yspec::ys_select(ysx_load_pkpdspec(), ID, TIME, EVID, DV, CMT)

data <- data.frame(
  ID = c(1, 1, 1, 2, 2),
  TIME = c(0, 1, 2, 0, 1),
  EVID = c(1, 0, 0, 1, 0),
  DV = c(-999, 5.1, 4.2, -999, 6.3),
  CMT = c(1, 2, 2, 1, 2)
)
```

The bundled specification marks `ID` as the group column and sets
`pre_grp_count: ~` (null), because a NONMEM data set has many rows per subject.
`DV` allows missing values, coded as `-999`.

## Run all checks

```{r check}
ysx_check(data, spec)
```

`ysx_check()` returns `TRUE` invisibly when everything passes. If any check
fails it prints every problem and stops. Use `error_on_fail = FALSE` to get
`FALSE` back instead.

```{r check-fail}
bad <- data
bad$CMT[2] <- -999
ysx_check(bad, spec, error_on_fail = FALSE)
```

Before it runs any check, `ysx_check()` asserts that the data and the
specification match: every column in `data` must be a variable in the
specification, and every specification variable must be a column in `data`.
With the default `error_on_fail = TRUE` a mismatch raises an error. With `FALSE`
it is reported with the other problems, and `error_on_fail` is also forwarded to
the individual checks. `ysx_check_missing()` is less strict: it only requires
the data columns to be in the specification.

## Missing values

`ysx_check_missing()` runs only the missing-value check and returns the
problems as a character vector. Every column in `data` must be described in the
specification, otherwise it raises an error (or returns a problem with
`error_on_fail = FALSE`). The specification may describe more columns than the
data has.

```{r missing}
ysx_check_missing(bad, spec)
```

Missing values are not allowed by default. Allow them for a column with
`dots: {na_ok: true}` in the YAML. If the specification has a `missing_code`,
a plain `NA` is a problem even when `na_ok` is true.

A second specification can be merged before checking with `spec2`. Columns that
exist in both keep the definition from `spec`.

```{r missing-spec2}
ysx_check_missing(
  data[c("ID", "DV")],
  yspec::ys_select(spec, ID),
  spec2 = yspec::ys_select(spec, DV)
)
```

## Repeats within groups

`ysx_check_repeats()` counts the rows in each group and stops if any group does
not have exactly `count` rows (default 1). It is the equivalent of grouping,
counting, and checking that no count differs from `count`. Missing values count
as a group value.

Pass the grouping columns with `groups` to avoid editing the specification. The
columns must exist in the specification.

```{r repeats-groups, error = TRUE}
ids <- data.frame(ID = c(1, 1, 2), TIME = c(0, 0, 0))
ysx_check_repeats(ids, spec, groups = c("ID", "TIME"))
```

With `error_on_fail = FALSE` the problems are returned instead:

```{r repeats-return}
ysx_check_repeats(ids, spec, groups = c("ID", "TIME"), error_on_fail = FALSE)
```

## Setting groups in the specification

`ysx_regroup()` removes all existing `group` settings and marks new ones.
`ysx_ungroup()` removes them all. Both return a new specification.

```{r regroup}
regrouped <- ysx_regroup(spec, c("ID", "TIME"))
names(Filter(function(x) isTRUE(x$dots$group), regrouped))

ungrouped <- ysx_ungroup(spec)
names(Filter(function(x) isTRUE(x$dots$group), ungrouped))
```

Within `ysx_check()`, the required number of rows per group comes from
`pre_grp_count` in the `dots` of the group columns:

| `pre_grp_count` | Meaning |
|---|---|
| not set | every group must have 1 row |
| a whole number `n` | every group must have `n` rows |
| `~`, `null`, or `None` | do not check repeats |

All group columns that set it must agree.
